recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Future changes to narrative safety or stronger requirements should be handled through a new tracker rather than by reapplying FHIR-7368.
issue_request: FHIR-7368 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core narrative issue asking to add that resource narrative may include extra human-edited content, but structured data should not contain information important to human readers that is omitted from narrative because receiving systems may not render non-narrative data.
initial_application: Converted source history shows commit 0a07e675b91532537fd767bf86070a433ced476f, '#7368 - note about narrative', adding the structured-data/narrative warning to source/narrative.html. Jira also records Grahame Grieve's application comment, 'svn revision 7368'. Later grammar cleanup f613e871f0b801b1e0a0dc2da3c509f287a5adcf retained the rule.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Narrative as an infrastructure type and maps narrative=narrative, confirming source/narrative.html is in build scope. Current source/narrative.html says resource instances that permit narrative SHOULD contain narrative as a fallback, structured data SHOULD NOT generally contain information important to human readers that is omitted from narrative, and creators should not assume systems will render or humans will see non-narrative data. FHIR-17688 later clarified the same paragraph's lead-in without reversing the rule, and FHIR-34041 later added narrative clinical-safety checklist guidance while declining stronger universal statements.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active narrative source already conveys the seed rule and later related decisions support keeping it as contextual SHOULD guidance.
